questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of angular velocity?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity is angular displacement per unit time, so it is measured in radians per second.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify units used to describe rotational motion.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is conserved when no external torque acts on a rotating system?
questions.explanation: A system with zero resultant external torque keeps a constant angular momentum.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall conservation of angular momentum in rotating systems.

questions.prompt: In simple harmonic motion, what is the direction of the restoring force?
options: Always opposite to the velocity only
questions.explanation: The restoring force in SHM is directed towards equilibrium and is proportional to displacement.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the restoring force that produces simple harmonic motion.

questions.prompt: How is gravitational field strength at a point defined?
options: Change in velocity per unit displacement
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength is the force that a unit mass would experience at that point.
questions.learningOutcome: Define gravitational field strength using force and mass.

questions.prompt: When does resonance occur in an oscillating system?
options: When the driving frequency equals the natural frequency
When friction is completely absent from every system
When the amplitude is forced to zero
When mass is removed from a stationary object
questions.correctAnswer: When the driving frequency equals the natural frequency
questions.explanation: Resonance produces a large response when the system is driven at its natural frequency.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize the condition for resonance in oscillating systems.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes electromagnetic waves in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves have electric and magnetic fields oscillating perpendicular to the direction of travel.
questions.learningOutcome: State the nature of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum.

questions.prompt: For two coherent waves, which path difference gives constructive interference?
options: An odd number of half wavelengths only
One quarter of a wavelength only
questions.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when waves arrive in phase, which happens for path differences of n lambda.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the path difference condition for constructive interference.

questions.prompt: What is the critical angle for light moving from glass to air?
options: The angle of incidence in glass for which the refracted ray is 90 degrees
The angle of reflection measured inside air
The angle at which light stops obeying reflection
The smallest angle made by a ray with a mirror surface
questions.correctAnswer: The angle of incidence in glass for which the refracted ray is 90 degrees
questions.explanation: The critical angle is measured in the optically denser medium when the refracted ray just grazes the boundary.
questions.learningOutcome: Define critical angle for light moving from a denser to a rarer medium.

questions.prompt: Which unit can be used for electric field strength?
questions.explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge, so newtons per coulomb is a correct unit.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify units of electric field strength.

questions.prompt: What does the capacitance of a capacitor measure?
options: Charge stored per unit potential difference
Current supplied per unit magnetic field
questions.correctAnswer: Charge stored per unit potential difference
questions.explanation: Capacitance is defined by C = Q/V, the charge stored for each volt across the capacitor.
questions.learningOutcome: Define capacitance in terms of charge and potential difference.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in webers, while magnetic flux density is measured in tesla.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the SI unit of magnetic flux.

questions.prompt: What does Lenz's law state about an induced current?
options: It flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it
It always flows clockwise around a coil
It is independent of magnetic flux change
questions.correctAnswer: It flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law is a conservation principle: the induced effect opposes the change in magnetic flux.
questions.learningOutcome: State Lenz's law for induced current direction.

questions.prompt: In the photoelectric effect, what is the work function of a metal?
options: The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from its surface
The maximum current through the metal wire
The power needed to heat the metal to melting point
The energy released by each radioactive nucleus
questions.correctAnswer: The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from its surface
questions.explanation: The work function is the least photon energy required to liberate an electron from a metal surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Define work function in photoelectric emission.

questions.prompt: What is meant by the half-life of a radioactive isotope?
options: Time taken for half the undecayed nuclei to decay
Time taken for all nuclei to become stable
Half the time needed to ionise an atom
Time taken for radiation to travel half a metre
questions.correctAnswer: Time taken for half the undecayed nuclei to decay
questions.explanation: Half-life measures the time for the number of undecayed radioactive nuclei to fall by half.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the meaning of radioactive half-life.

questions.prompt: What is the main action of a semiconductor diode in a simple circuit?
options: It allows current more easily in one direction than the other
It converts sound directly into nuclear energy
It makes resistance zero at room temperature
questions.correctAnswer: It allows current more easily in one direction than the other
questions.explanation: A diode has a low resistance in forward bias and a high resistance in reverse bias.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the rectifying action of a semiconductor diode.

questions.prompt: A projectile moves without air resistance. What happens to its horizontal velocity after launch?
options: It reverses at the highest point
questions.explanation: With no horizontal resultant force, the horizontal component of velocity remains unchanged.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain horizontal motion of a projectile in the absence of air resistance.

questions.prompt: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle. In which direction is the centripetal force on the stone?
options: Towards the centre of the circle
Along the tangent in the direction of motion
Away from the centre of the circle
questions.correctAnswer: Towards the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is the resultant force directed towards the centre that changes the direction of velocity.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the direction of centripetal force in circular motion.

questions.prompt: For a satellite in a stable circular orbit around Earth, what provides the centripetal force?
options: Air resistance from the upper atmosphere only
A permanent outward force from the orbit
questions.explanation: Gravity acts towards Earth's centre and supplies the centripetal force needed for orbital motion.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate gravitational force to satellite circular motion.

questions.prompt: Which set of factors determines the pressure at a point in a liquid at rest?
options: Density, gravitational field strength, and depth
Container colour, surface area, and volume
Mass of the container, current, and voltage
questions.correctAnswer: Density, gravitational field strength, and depth
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure at depth h is given by p = rho g h, so density, g, and depth are the relevant factors.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the factors affecting pressure in a liquid.

questions.prompt: A falling raindrop reaches terminal velocity. Which statement best explains this motion?
options: Upward resistive forces balance its weight
Gravity has stopped acting on it
Its acceleration is greater than g
questions.correctAnswer: Upward resistive forces balance its weight
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero, so the object continues at constant speed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain terminal velocity using balanced forces.

questions.prompt: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s and has a frequency of 680 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explanation: Using v = f lambda, lambda = 340/680 = 0.50 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the wave equation to calculate wavelength.

questions.prompt: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz. What is its period?
questions.explanation: The period is T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.020 s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate wave period from frequency.

questions.prompt: Light travels at 3.0 x 10^8 m/s in a vacuum and 2.0 x 10^8 m/s in glass. What is the refractive index of the glass?
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v = 3.0 x 10^8 divided by 2.0 x 10^8 = 1.5.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate refractive index from speed of light in a medium.

questions.prompt: A converging lens forms an image of an object placed beyond its focal length. Which image description is generally correct?
questions.explanation: For an object beyond the focal length of a converging lens, refracted rays meet to form a real inverted image.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe image formation by a converging lens.

questions.prompt: Which condition is required for total internal reflection?
options: Light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle
Light travels from air to glass at any angle
The angle of incidence is zero degrees in all media
The reflecting surface is painted black
questions.correctAnswer: Light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs a denser-to-rarer boundary and an incidence angle greater than the critical angle.
questions.learningOutcome: State the conditions needed for total internal reflection.

questions.prompt: Two resistors of 3 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series. What is their combined resistance?
questions.explanation: Series resistances add directly, so R = 3 + 5 = 8 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate equivalent resistance for resistors in series.

questions.prompt: A 6 ohm resistor and a 3 ohm resistor are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate equivalent resistance for two parallel resistors.

questions.prompt: What current flows through a 4 ohm resistor connected to a 12 V supply?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.
questions.learningOutcome: Use Ohm's law to calculate current.

questions.prompt: A current of 2 A flows for 5 minutes. How much charge passes a point in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Convert 5 minutes to 300 s, then Q = It = 2 x 300 = 600 C.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate electric charge transferred by a steady current.

questions.prompt: A device connected to 240 V draws a current of 0.50 A. What is its power?
questions.explanation: Electrical power is P = VI = 240 x 0.50 = 120 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate power from potential difference and current.

questions.prompt: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: Concentric circles centred on the wire
Straight lines parallel to the wire only
Radial lines pointing away from one end
questions.correctAnswer: Concentric circles centred on the wire
questions.explanation: A straight current-carrying conductor produces circular magnetic field lines around the wire.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the magnetic field pattern around a straight current-carrying conductor.

questions.prompt: Which change increases the force on a straight current-carrying conductor placed at right angles to a magnetic field?
options: Increasing the current in the conductor
Reducing the conductor length to zero
Replacing the conductor with dry wood
questions.correctAnswer: Increasing the current in the conductor
questions.explanation: The force is F = BIL for a conductor at right angles, so increasing current increases the force.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate conductor force to current in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: What energy conversion occurs in an electric generator?
questions.explanation: A generator uses electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical work into electrical energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify energy conversion in an electric generator.

questions.prompt: A transformer has more turns on its secondary coil than on its primary coil. What type of transformer is it?
questions.explanation: More turns on the secondary coil than the primary coil gives a higher secondary voltage.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a step-up transformer from its coil turns.

questions.prompt: How does photon energy change when the frequency of light increases?
options: It stays fixed for all colours
It depends only on the source size
questions.explanation: Photon energy is E = hf, so higher frequency means higher energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate photon energy to frequency.

questions.prompt: Light below the threshold frequency shines on a clean metal surface. What happens in the photoelectric effect?
options: Photoelectrons are emitted after a long delay
questions.explanation: If photon frequency is below threshold, each photon has too little energy to release an electron.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of threshold frequency in photoelectric emission.

questions.prompt: What is an alpha particle?
questions.explanation: An alpha particle contains two protons and two neutrons, the same as a helium nucleus.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify alpha radiation by its particle composition.

questions.prompt: Which description matches nuclear fission?
options: A heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei and releases energy
Two light nuclei combine only at room temperature
An atom gains an electron in a chemical bond
A magnet loses its north pole permanently
questions.correctAnswer: A heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei and releases energy
questions.explanation: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus, often releasing neutrons and a large amount of energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish nuclear fission from other nuclear and chemical changes.

questions.prompt: Which practice best reduces random error when measuring the period of a pendulum?
options: Time many oscillations and repeat the measurement
Use only one swing and round to the nearest second
Start timing before releasing the pendulum
Change the length during the measurement
questions.correctAnswer: Time many oscillations and repeat the measurement
questions.explanation: Timing several oscillations and repeating reduces the effect of reaction-time variation on the mean period.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose methods that reduce random error in timing experiments.

questions.prompt: For an ohmic conductor, what does the gradient of a potential difference against current graph represent?
questions.explanation: For a V against I graph, the gradient is V/I, which equals resistance for an ohmic conductor.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret gradients from electrical measurement graphs.

questions.prompt: A car speeds up uniformly from 10 m/s to 25 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity divided by time: (25 - 10)/5 = 3 m/s^2.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate acceleration from a change in velocity over time.

questions.prompt: A resultant force gives a 2.0 kg trolley an acceleration of 4.0 m/s^2. What is the resultant force?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives F = ma = 2.0 x 4.0 = 8 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Newton's second law to calculate resultant force.

questions.prompt: Using g = 10 N/kg, how much work is done in lifting a 5 kg mass vertically through 2 m?
questions.explanation: Work done against gravity is mgh = 5 x 10 x 2 = 100 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate work done against gravity.

questions.prompt: A machine does 600 J of useful work in 20 s. What is its useful power output?
questions.explanation: Power is work done per unit time: P = 600/20 = 30 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate power from useful work and time.

questions.prompt: What is the momentum of a 0.40 kg ball moving at 15 m/s?
questions.explanation: Momentum is p = mv = 0.40 x 15 = 6.0 kg m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate linear momentum from mass and velocity.

questions.prompt: A 0.15 kg ball changes velocity from 30 m/s east to 20 m/s west after hitting a wall. What is the magnitude of its change in momentum?
questions.explanation: Taking east as positive, change in velocity is -20 - 30 = -50 m/s, so the magnitude of change in momentum is 0.15 x 50 = 7.5 kg m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate change in momentum when velocity reverses direction.

questions.prompt: A cyclist moves round a circular track of radius 3 m at 9 m/s. What is the centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is a = v^2/r = 9^2/3 = 27 m/s^2.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate centripetal acceleration from speed and radius.

questions.prompt: A spring has a spring constant of 200 N/m. What force is needed to extend it by 0.050 m within its elastic limit?
questions.explanation: Hooke's law gives F = kx = 200 x 0.050 = 10 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Use Hooke's law to calculate force on a spring.

questions.prompt: A 0.50 kg mass oscillates on a spring of spring constant 200 N/m. Using pi = 3.14, what is the approximate period?
questions.explanation: T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k) = 2 x 3.14 x sqrt(0.50/200), which is about 0.31 s.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the mass-spring period formula for simple harmonic motion.

questions.prompt: Using g = 10 N/kg, what gravitational potential energy is gained by a 1500 kg lift raised through 20 m?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy gained is mgh = 1500 x 10 x 20 = 300000 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate gravitational potential energy for vertical lifting.

questions.prompt: A wave has wavelength 0.75 m and frequency 8 Hz. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: The wave speed is v = f lambda = 8 x 0.75 = 6.0 m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate wave speed from frequency and wavelength.

questions.prompt: An echo is heard 0.60 s after a shout. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far away is the reflecting wall?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the wall and back, so distance to the wall is vt/2 = 340 x 0.60 / 2 = 102 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Use echo timing to calculate distance.

questions.prompt: In a double-slit experiment, wavelength is 6.0 x 10^-7 m, screen distance is 2.0 m, and slit separation is 3.0 x 10^-4 m. What is the fringe spacing?
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing x = lambda D/a = (6.0 x 10^-7 x 2.0)/(3.0 x 10^-4) = 4.0 x 10^-3 m, or 4.0 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate fringe spacing in a double-slit interference pattern.

questions.prompt: An object is 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the image distance?
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the thin lens formula to calculate image distance.

questions.prompt: An object is 30 cm from a lens and its real image is 15 cm from the lens. What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of magnification is v/u = 15/30 = 0.50.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate magnification from object and image distances.

questions.prompt: A charge of 6 C passes a point in a wire in 3 s. What is the current?
questions.explanation: Current is charge per unit time, I = Q/t = 6/3 = 2 A.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate current from charge flow and time.

questions.prompt: A resistor carries 3 A when the potential difference across it is 9 V. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is R = V/I = 9/3 = 3 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate resistance from potential difference and current.

questions.prompt: A 1000 W heater is used for 2 hours. How much electrical energy is used?
questions.explanation: Energy in kilowatt-hours is power in kilowatts multiplied by time in hours: 1 kW x 2 h = 2 kWh.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate electrical energy consumption in kilowatt-hours.

questions.prompt: Two lamps are connected in series to a battery. Which statement about the current is correct?
options: The same current passes through both lamps
The first lamp uses up all the current
Current is zero between the lamps
The larger lamp must carry twice the current
questions.correctAnswer: The same current passes through both lamps
questions.explanation: In a series circuit there is only one conducting path, so the same current passes through each component.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply current rules for components in series.

questions.prompt: A 2 k ohm resistor and a 4 k ohm resistor are connected in series across 12 V. What is the potential difference across the 4 k ohm resistor?
questions.explanation: Voltage divides in proportion to resistance, so the 4 k ohm resistor gets 4/(2 + 4) x 12 = 8 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the potential divider rule for two series resistors.

questions.prompt: A 200 uF capacitor is connected to a 12 V supply. How much charge is stored when fully charged?
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate charge stored by a capacitor.

questions.prompt: What energy is stored in a 100 uF capacitor charged to 20 V?
questions.explanation: Energy stored is E = 1/2 CV^2 = 0.5 x 100 x 10^-6 x 20^2 = 0.020 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate energy stored in a charged capacitor.

questions.prompt: A 0.20 m wire carries 5 A at right angles to a 0.40 T magnetic field. What force acts on the wire?
questions.explanation: The motor-effect force is F = BIL = 0.40 x 5 x 0.20 = 0.40 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: The magnetic flux through a 50-turn coil changes by 0.020 Wb in 0.10 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Faraday's law gives emf = N deltaPhi/delta t = 50 x 0.020/0.10 = 10 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate induced emf from rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.

questions.prompt: A transformer has 600 primary turns and 1200 secondary turns. If the primary voltage is 240 V, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 1200/600 = 2, so Vs = 480 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the transformer turns ratio to calculate secondary voltage.

questions.prompt: An alternating current has a period of 0.010 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is f = 1/T = 1/0.010 = 100 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate alternating-current frequency from period.

questions.prompt: A photon of energy 5 eV strikes a metal with work function 2 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy of an emitted photoelectron?
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy is photon energy minus work function: 5 eV - 2 eV = 3 eV.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the photoelectric equation to calculate maximum kinetic energy.

questions.prompt: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 6 hours. If it starts with 80 g, how much remains undecayed after 18 hours?
questions.explanation: Eighteen hours is three half-lives, so 80 g becomes 40 g, then 20 g, then 10 g.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply half-life to find the remaining undecayed mass.

questions.prompt: A detector records 460 counts per minute from a source and background together. The background count is 40 counts per minute. What is the corrected source count rate?
questions.explanation: Subtract the background count from the total count: 460 - 40 = 420 counts per minute.
questions.learningOutcome: Correct radioactive count rate measurements for background radiation.

questions.prompt: A spring extends by 0.040 m when an 8.0 N load is attached. What is the spring constant?
questions.learningOutcome: Use force-extension measurements to calculate spring constant.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched with an initial vertical velocity of 20 m/s. Using g = 10 m/s^2, what is its maximum height above the launch point?
questions.explanation: At maximum height vertical velocity is zero, so h = u^2/(2g) = 20^2/(2 x 10) = 20 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze vertical projectile motion to calculate maximum height.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg trolley moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley and they stick together. What is their common speed after collision?
questions.explanation: Momentum before is 2 x 6 = 12 kg m/s. Combined mass is 3 kg, so speed after collision is 12/3 = 4 m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conservation of momentum for a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.prompt: In the collision where a 2 kg trolley at 6 m/s sticks to a stationary 1 kg trolley, how much kinetic energy is lost?
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is 0.5 x 2 x 6^2 = 36 J. Final kinetic energy is 0.5 x 3 x 4^2 = 24 J, so 12 J is lost.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare kinetic energy before and after an inelastic collision.

questions.prompt: A vehicle moves round a banked curve of radius 50 m. If tan theta = 0.20 and g = 10 m/s^2, what speed needs no sideways friction?
questions.explanation: For a banked curve without sideways friction, v = sqrt(rg tan theta) = sqrt(50 x 10 x 0.20) = 10 m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze forces on a vehicle moving round a banked curve.

questions.prompt: If gravitational field strength at Earth's surface is g, what is its approximate value at a distance 2R from Earth's centre, where R is Earth's radius?
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength follows an inverse-square relationship, so doubling distance from the centre gives one quarter of the surface value.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the inverse-square relationship for gravitational field strength.

questions.prompt: An engineer adds dampers to a bridge that may be forced by periodic wind gusts. What is the main purpose of the dampers?
options: To make the bridge mass zero
To increase the wind frequency only
To remove gravitational force from the bridge
questions.explanation: Damping dissipates energy, reducing the amplitude that can build up when the driving frequency is near resonance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how damping controls resonance in structures.

questions.prompt: A string fixed at both ends is 1.2 m long. If wave speed on the string is 120 m/s, what is the fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For the fundamental mode of a string fixed at both ends, lambda = 2L = 2.4 m, so f = 120/2.4 = 50 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate fundamental frequency for a stretched string.

questions.prompt: A pipe closed at one end is 0.85 m long. Taking sound speed as 340 m/s, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For a pipe closed at one end, the fundamental wavelength is 4L = 3.4 m, so f = 340/3.4 = 100 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate fundamental frequency for a closed pipe.

questions.prompt: A water wave passes through a gap. When is diffraction most noticeable?
options: When the gap width is comparable to the wavelength
When the gap is infinitely wider than the wavelength
When the wave has zero amplitude
When the water is completely still
questions.correctAnswer: When the gap width is comparable to the wavelength
questions.explanation: Diffraction is strongest when an aperture or obstacle has a size similar to the wavelength.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how aperture size affects diffraction.

questions.prompt: Two thin lenses in contact have powers +5 D and -2 D. What is the combined focal length?
questions.explanation: Lens powers add, so total power is +3 D. Focal length f = 1/P = 1/3 m, about 0.33 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze combined power and focal length of lenses in contact.

questions.prompt: A cell of emf 12 V has terminal potential difference 10 V when delivering 2 A. What is its internal resistance?
questions.explanation: Lost volts are E - V = 2 V. Since lost volts = Ir, r = 2/2 = 1 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate internal resistance from emf, terminal voltage, and current.

questions.prompt: A 12 V supply is connected across 2 ohm and 4 ohm resistors in series. What is the power dissipated in the 4 ohm resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 6 ohm, so current is 2 A. Power in the 4 ohm resistor is I^2R = 2^2 x 4 = 16 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze a series circuit to calculate component power.

questions.prompt: A balanced Wheatstone bridge has ratio arms 2 ohm and 3 ohm, and one lower arm is 4 ohm. What resistance must the other lower arm have for balance?
questions.explanation: For balance, P/Q = R/S. With 2/3 = 4/S, S = 6 ohm.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the Wheatstone bridge balance condition.

questions.prompt: A 20 uF capacitor is charged through a 100 k ohm resistor. What is the time constant of the circuit?
questions.explanation: The time constant is RC = 100000 x 20 x 10^-6 = 2.0 s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the time constant for a resistor-capacitor circuit.

questions.prompt: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 325 V. What is its approximate rms value?
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal supply, Vrms = Vpeak/sqrt(2), so 325/sqrt(2) is approximately 230 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate peak and rms values of a sinusoidal voltage.

questions.prompt: A straight conductor of length 0.40 m moves at 8 m/s at right angles to a 0.50 T magnetic field. What emf is induced across its ends?
questions.explanation: Motional emf is E = Blv = 0.50 x 0.40 x 8 = 1.6 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate emf induced in a conductor moving through a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: The north pole of a magnet is pushed towards a coil connected to a galvanometer. What polarity is induced at the near face of the coil?
options: No pole because the magnet is moving
Alternating north and south every half turn
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, the induced current opposes the approaching north pole, so the near face of the coil becomes a north pole.
questions.learningOutcome: Predict induced polarity using Lenz's law.

questions.prompt: A photoelectron has maximum kinetic energy 3.2 x 10^-19 J. Using e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, what stopping potential is needed?
questions.explanation: Stopping potential satisfies eV = KE, so V = 3.2 x 10^-19 / 1.6 x 10^-19 = 2.0 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate stopping potential from maximum photoelectron kinetic energy.

questions.prompt: The momentum of a particle is doubled. What happens to its de Broglie wavelength?
questions.explanation: The de Broglie wavelength is lambda = h/p, so doubling momentum halves the wavelength.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the inverse relationship between particle momentum and de Broglie wavelength.

questions.prompt: A radioactive count rate falls from 800 counts per minute to 100 counts per minute in 12 days. What is the half-life?
questions.explanation: The count rate changes 800 to 400 to 200 to 100, which is three half-lives in 12 days. Each half-life is 4 days.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze count-rate changes to determine half-life.

questions.prompt: Which plan best determines g using a simple pendulum in a school laboratory?
options: Measure several lengths, time many oscillations for each, then plot T^2 against length
Measure one swing at one length and divide the length by the time
Use any mass and assume the period equals the mass
Pull the bob through 90 degrees and record the largest speed
questions.correctAnswer: Measure several lengths, time many oscillations for each, then plot T^2 against length
questions.explanation: For a simple pendulum, T^2 = 4 pi^2 L/g, so a T^2 against L graph gives a reliable gradient for finding g.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a graph-based method for determining gravitational field strength.

questions.prompt: Which method best finds the internal resistance of a cell from experimental data?
options: Vary the load, measure terminal voltage and current, then use the gradient of a V against I graph
Measure only the open-circuit voltage once
Connect the cell directly across an ammeter for a long time
Measure the mass of the cell before and after use
questions.correctAnswer: Vary the load, measure terminal voltage and current, then use the gradient of a V against I graph
questions.explanation: For a cell, V = E - Ir, so the negative gradient of terminal voltage against current gives internal resistance.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an investigation to determine emf and internal resistance.

questions.prompt: Which observation is strongest evidence that light transfers energy in photons rather than only as a classical wave?
options: Photoelectrons are emitted only above a threshold frequency
Water waves diffract around a barrier
A plane mirror forms a virtual image
questions.correctAnswer: Photoelectrons are emitted only above a threshold frequency
questions.explanation: A threshold frequency shows that each electron needs one photon with enough energy, which classical wave intensity alone cannot explain.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate experimental evidence for the photon model of light.

questions.prompt: Why do crumple zones in vehicles reduce injury risk during a collision?
options: They increase collision time, reducing average force for the same change in momentum
They make momentum disappear before impact
They remove the need for seat belts
They increase acceleration so passengers stop sooner
questions.correctAnswer: They increase collision time, reducing average force for the same change in momentum
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. Increasing the stopping time reduces the average force on passengers.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safety features using impulse and momentum principles.

questions.prompt: For long-distance power transmission at fixed power, why are step-up transformers used near power stations?
options: They raise voltage and lower current, reducing I^2R losses in cables
They make cable resistance exactly zero
They convert alternating current into radioactive energy
They lower voltage so current becomes larger in the lines
questions.correctAnswer: They raise voltage and lower current, reducing I^2R losses in cables
questions.explanation: For the same transmitted power, higher voltage means lower current, and cable heating losses are proportional to I^2R.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate transformer use in efficient electrical power transmission.

questions.prompt: A battery-powered lamp becomes very dim when switched on, and the terminal voltage of the battery drops sharply under load. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The battery has a large internal resistance
The circuit current is alternating at high frequency
The voltmeter is measuring gravitational field strength
questions.correctAnswer: The battery has a large internal resistance
questions.explanation: A large internal resistance causes a large lost voltage Ir inside the battery, leaving less terminal voltage for the lamp.
questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose circuit behaviour using internal resistance concepts.

questions.prompt: A rectifier output has too much ripple for a small DC device. Which design change would best smooth the output?
options: Add a larger capacitor in parallel with the load
Remove all diodes from the rectifier
Connect the load only to an open switch
Replace the capacitor with an air gap
questions.correctAnswer: Add a larger capacitor in parallel with the load
questions.explanation: A larger smoothing capacitor stores more charge and discharges more slowly between peaks, reducing ripple.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a circuit design change to improve rectified DC output.

questions.prompt: What is the role of control rods in a nuclear fission reactor?
options: They absorb neutrons to control the chain reaction rate
They provide all the uranium fuel
They reflect visible light into the turbine
They turn gamma rays directly into steam
questions.correctAnswer: They absorb neutrons to control the chain reaction rate
questions.explanation: Control rods absorb excess neutrons, allowing operators to slow or maintain the fission chain reaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate how reactor components control nuclear fission.

questions.prompt: A learner measures very small wire extensions using single load readings and gets scattered results. Which improvement best increases reliability?
options: Take readings for several loads and use the gradient of a force-extension graph
Use fewer readings to finish faster
Record extensions only to the nearest metre
Change the wire material after every reading
questions.correctAnswer: Take readings for several loads and use the gradient of a force-extension graph
questions.explanation: A graph uses all data points, reduces the effect of scatter, and gives a more reliable stiffness estimate than one reading.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate experimental improvements for reliable elasticity measurements.

questions.prompt: Which investigation design can determine the speed of sound most directly using electronic timing?
options: Place two microphones a known distance apart and measure the time delay of the same sound pulse
Measure the colour of a loudspeaker cone while it vibrates
Time one hand clap with a stopwatch held next to the source
Weigh a tuning fork before and after it sounds
questions.correctAnswer: Place two microphones a known distance apart and measure the time delay of the same sound pulse
questions.explanation: With microphone separation d and measured time delay t, the sound speed is found directly from v = d/t.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an electronic timing method to determine the speed of sound.
